title: Niryasa 3. The Description of the Glory of Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja
html:
Hemalata's account: Srinivasa's three-day samadhi in Vishnupura — as Mani Manjari he searches for Sri Radha's nose-ring, lost in the water-pastimes in the Yamuna; Ishvari's account of Ramachandra's obedience (the meal from the guru's plate, the 'snake' and Arjuna's example) and of the meal with Narottama; Ramachandra enters meditation and finds the ring; the remnants from Radha's lips

1Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya and Nityananda!
Glory to Advaita-chandra, glory to Gaura's devotees!

2I shall tell another narrative — listen attentively;
I shall tell something confidential — fill your ears with it.

3By hearing it bliss arises in the heart;
what can I, most unworthy, say of it?

4Listen, listen, devotees, to the greatness of Ramachandra,
by singing whose virtues prema arises in the heart.

5One day my mistress, Srila Hemalata,
graciously began to tell me this.

6What I heard from the lips of Srimati
filled my heart with joy.

7Touching with my ears the ocean of Sri Ramachandra's greatness,
I floated in bliss, in great jubilation.

8Prabhu and Ramachandra are as if one body;
his heart is deep, he is a great and composed devotee.

9What sweet beauty, what sweetness of character!
All the virtues I heard of are wondrous.

10Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja knows Prabhu's heart —
this is manifest to the whole world.

11Sri Ramachandra's deeds are renowned in the world,
his gentleness and depth are famous throughout the universe.

12Of this I shall tell a little, making it known,
touching only one particle for my own purification.

13One day, in the house at Vana-Vishnupura,
Prabhu was seated with a joyful heart.

14The two Ishvaris1 sit on either side of him
and blissfully gaze on Prabhu's form.

15Both greatly praised their good fortune:
"Such lotus feet of Prabhu we have obtained by great fortune!"

16Then Prabhu speaks of Krishna in supreme bliss,
and hearing it, the Ishvaris' joy increased.

17Thus for some time, in the rasa of talk about Krishna,
Prabhu was immersed in great jubilation of prema.

18His mind, overflowing with bhava, cannot grow calm;
tears, trembling and gooseflesh pervade his body.

19Now he roars and rolls on the ground,
now he cries out and calls aloud.

20Saying "Sri Gauranga-chandra", he faints again and again;
helpless in transport, he cries, "Alas, alas!"

21Now he calls aloud, "Sri Rupa, Sanatana!"
Saying "Sri Bhatta Gosani", he floats in the happiness of prema.

22When some time had passed in this way,
in talk of other things Prabhu's mind grew calm.

23Then, after a while, he bathed,
put on white cloth and sat down on his seat.

24Applying tilaka to his forehead and the letters of the holy names to his body,
Prabhu recites hymns in a beautiful voice.

25How the sound of his voice surpasses the kokila!
Joyful at heart, Prabhu recites the hymns.

26With a joyful heart, seated on his seat,
Prabhu carefully serves Sri Vamshivadana.2

27Having performed the service with sandal and tulasi
and offered it, Prabhu sat down to meditate.

28Fixing his mind in the siddha-deha of his cherished service,
he beholds the wondrous sweetness of the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.3

29He beholds the water-pastimes of Radha and Krishna,
and seeing that lila his mind is immersed in happiness.

30In the Yamuna, skilfully arranging the water-sport,
They advanced against each other in a water-battle.

31All the gopis surrounded Krishnachandra —
as though a host of lightning-flashes surrounded a cloud.

32All the ornaments on their bodies they gave to the maidservants
and entered the water, saying, "We shall defeat Krishna!"

33The sakhis devoted to service, remaining on the bank,
fill their eyes with the beauty of the forms of the Two.

34Sri Rupa Manjari and Lavanga Manjari,
Sri Guna Manjari and Sri Rati Manjari,

35Sri Rasa Manjari and Vilasa Manjari,
Sri Manjulali and all the other manjaris —

36all of them, standing behind, watch
and calmly behold the lila.

37All together they girded their garments tightly at the waist
and bound their hair very firmly.

38When the battle began,
They began to speak with great boasting.

39And as soon as the water-battle began,
(Radha) unnoticed splashed water in Sri Krishna's face.

40What movements of Her body, what swaying of Her waist!
What movements of Her hands, what play of Her brows!

41What grace of motion, what gait!
Immersed, She showers Him with water without end.

42What wondrous movement of Her breast,
what sweetness in the slight turn of Her neck!

43Every now and then, the play of brows and waves of words,
and waves of Her voice surpassing the ocean of nectar.

44Then fair-faced Radha with Her sakhis
splashes water, aiming at Krishna's eyes.

45What hundreds of endless ruses therein!
What movement of the water — the limit of expertise!

46All shower Him with water, joyful at heart,
as the clouds of Shravana pour down rain.

47A smile on Her lips — in it an ocean of loveliness:
the moon Krishna sank in the ocean of nectar.

48Now they fight in water up to the knees, now up to the waist,
now up to the breast, now up to the neck.4

49Now they fight face to face, now breast to breast,
now eye to eye, now nail to nail.

50Now it is a battle of words, now hand to hand;
all are spent in the play, intoxicated with bliss.

51So the water-battle grew boundlessly:
with daring they drive the water at each other.

52Then Krishna stole the garments of all;
in the clear water of the Yamuna their bodies are seen.

53What grace of limbs, what waves of loveliness!
Bliss grows in the heart, waves of happiness.

54This water-pastime is fathomless and boundless:
how can a living being of small intelligence comprehend it?

55It is described at length in the Sri Govinda-lilamrita:
Kaviraja Gosani depicted it there.5

56Helpless with bliss, Radha forgot Herself,
and at that moment the ornament of Her nose slipped off.6

57Having finished the pastime, all came up on the bank;
the sakhis devoted to service rejoiced.

58Dressing each in her own garments and ornaments,
they joyfully admire the beauty of their forms.

59Then the happy Sweet-faced One with the sakhis
entered the bower-house together with Krishna.

60At once all the foods prepared by Vrinda were brought;
seeing the fare, all rejoiced at heart.

61Arranging various fruits,
(Radha), seeing the fare, was immersed in bliss.

62How many kinds of sweets and various dishes!
Both taste them, immersed in bliss.

63The sakhis devoted to service serve:
each performs her own service.

64Seeing the sweetness of the forms of the Two,
the sakhis, gazing on Their beauty, forget themselves.

65What essence of loveliness the Creator has made!
What sweetness — an ocean of nectar, the limit of beauty!

66With what, brothers, can I compare this beauty,
this grace of form — the limit of sweetness?

67I look for a comparison — there is none:
the beauty of Their holy forms is comparable only to itself.

68The Creator kneaded it from the essence of nectar;
millions of moons are offered up to the beauty of Their faces.

69Then, gazing at Radha's moon-like face,
they see: the nose is bare — where is the nose-ornament?

70"Has it fallen into the water during the play?" —
all were troubled about the ornament.

71They all took counsel with one another;
their hearts were anxious about the nose-ring.

72Then Sri Rupa Manjari speaks by a sign,
casting a glance at Sri Guna Manjari.

73Sri Guna Manjari, making a sign,
speaks with pleasure to Mani Manjari:7

74"You, dear one, are virtuous and know Radha's heart;
how many times you have brought Radha's ornaments!

75Sometimes the play is in the water of the kunda, sometimes in water up to the breast,
sometimes the play is by day, sometimes at night —

76so many times you have brought back ornaments.
Now find it and bring it — this is my word."

77Then Mani Manjari, receiving the order,
joyfully went to search.

78Coming to the bank of the Yamuna, she looked;
not finding it on the bank, she entered the water.

79She gazes into the clear water of the Yamuna,
but cannot see the nose-ornament.

80The water shines like a mirror,
the rays of the sun sparkle in it.

81She searched a long time but could not find it,
and, not finding it, was pained at heart.

82During the play in the water the Two had fought many battles —
both most expert, both most discerning.

83In the Yamuna are enchanting footprints,
and among them the nose-ring had fallen.

84Covered by a lotus leaf, it was not noticed;
not finding the ornament, she became anxious.

85White sand and a white leaf
had covered it — that is why it was not seen.

86Thus, having searched for a long time,
she reflected with a sorrowful heart.

87Meanwhile the two Sri Ishvaris, looking at Prabhu,
began to speak in great anxiety.

88From the first prahara of the day until evening
so much time has passed, and Prabhu's meditation does not end.

89They saw that his whole body had grown stiff,
and both recalled the states of Mahaprabhu.

90There is no breathing in or out, the belly does not move;
seeing this, both lost heart.

91How loudly they shouted into his ears —
but he does not regain consciousness, even hearing the cries of "Hari!"

92When the first prahara of the night had passed in this way,
the Ishvaris' grief grew in their hearts.

93How many forebodings rose in their minds:
"Surely now the Creator has become merciless to me!"

94They beat their breasts and roll on the ground;
"What have you done, Creator!" they cry, "Alas, alas!"

95Now, calming themselves for a moment and taking heart,
both fan him very gently with the end of their cloth.

96Hearing that Prabhu does not come out of his meditation, the king
came quickly, in great haste.

97The king came to Prabhu's house with an anxious heart
and many times prostrated himself on the ground with eight limbs.

98Then the king saw an even deeper state;
seeing it, the king grew sorrowful at heart.

99Such an expression of bhava he had never heard of;
he holds a finger to his nose and cries, "Alas, alas!"

100The king came and sat near the Thakurani
and began to question the two Srimatis.

101The Thakurani says, "Listen, I shall tell you,"
and began to describe his state to him:

102"He sat down to meditate in the first prahara of the day…"
From the lips of Srimati the king learned everything.

103The king, in great anxiety, looks for a remedy;
sighing deeply, the king cries, "Alas, alas!"

104At that moment Sri Vallavi Kaviraja came
and bowed to the Ishvari, prostrate on the ground.

105Then Sri Vyasacharya, Sri Krishnavallabha,
Janaki Dasa and Prasada Dasa all came.

106Seeing Prabhu, all were saddened
and, hanging their heads, began to ponder.

107They tried in every way — he does not regain consciousness;
seeing that the meditation does not break, they lost heart.

108The third prahara of the night passed;
crying "Alas, alas!", they wept much:

109"Alas, cruel Creator, what have you done!" —
they beat their breasts, rolling on the ground.

110"Now the Creator has become cruel to me!" —
crying "Alas, alas!", how they weep.

111Then Prabhu's devotees gathered together
and began to speak in great anxiety:

112"Listen, listen, Thakurani! Calm your heart:
our Prabhu is absorbed in bhava — he will regain consciousness."

113Both grew a little calmer, restraining their grief,
and, taking heart, sat down beside Prabhu.

114All together they reflect in their minds:
by no means does Prabhu's meditation break.

115So the night passed and day came;
endlessly they wondered how to break the meditation.

116The king and all Prabhu's devotees
reflect with sorrowful hearts.

117Thus they fell into many thoughts —
the third prahara of the day began.

118Still there is no movement; grief is in their hearts,
and in their minds unceasing forebodings:

119"Alas, alas, what shall we do, where shall we go?
Where shall we find such a treasure of virtues?"

120Pained at heart, all lament:
"Surely the cruel Creator has brought calamity."

121So that day too passed,
and the third day began.

122Loud wailing arose;
falling, they dash themselves on the ground.

123Restraining herself and taking heart, the Thakurani
held cotton to his nose and watches.

124When she saw that the cotton at his nose did not stir,
she tore her hair and fell, striking the ground.

125Rolling on the ground, she cries, "Alas, alas!";
she beats her breast and weeps aloud.

126Now she rises, now falls, now loses consciousness,
now wails and weeps.

127Thus they began to lament;
all were distraught and lost their strength:

128"Ah, ah, pitiless, cruel Creator!
Why have you taken away the limit of our happiness?

129Having given the treasure of mercy, why have you taken it away?
Having given a great jewel, you have snatched it back!"

130Then Srimati-jiu reflects within herself,
and as she reflects, she remembers a certain word.

131Her heart brightened, her face brightened,
and she began to speak with joy.

132The devotees all together entreat her:
"Tell us, tell us, Thakurani, what is in your mind?"

133The king and all came closer:
"Tell us and calm us — we are in distress."

134Then Srimati speaks with joy:
"Listen gladly, all you devotees.

135What I heard earlier from Prabhu's lips,
all that has now come back to my mind.

136Ramachandra Kaviraja knows the truth about Prabhu;
no one else knows the thoughts of Prabhu's heart.

137If he comes, then there will be joy."
And she began to tell, very softly:

138The Thakurani says: "Listen. One day Prabhu
was speaking of the Kaviraja's virtues:

139'He is the limit of composure, his bhajana is profound;
that great and steadfast one knows my mind.

140All the movements of my heart the Kaviraja knows;
I dreamt that the Kaviraja would come today.'

141This he said again and again with joy —
and just then Ramachandra arrived in supreme bliss.

142Seeing Prabhu, he fell to the ground and bowed,
and with joined palms offered many praises.

143Prabhu rose and embraced him
and began to ask about his welfare.

144The Kaviraja says: 'Without the sight of you,
without the sight of your feet, what welfare can there be?

145Now good fortune has come — I have obtained your sight;
I have attained my goal, my life is fruitful.'

146Taking the Kaviraja by the hand, Prabhu
joyfully seated him beside him.

147Some time passed in talk of Krishna;
at the sight of each other the joy of both increased.

148Then after a while both bathed
and, reciting hymns, came back.

149Now he calls aloud, 'Gaurachandra!',
now, saying 'Rupa, Sanatana!', sheds tears;

150now, saying 'Sri Bhatta Gosani!', cries out;
every now and then he exclaims, 'Radha-Govinda!'

151Thus Prabhu came back after bathing,
went to Sri Vamshivadana and bowed down;

152he changed his cloth, applied tilaka,
and calls again and again, 'Sri Kunda! Govardhana!'

153Then, joyful, performing his daily duties,
he gladly went to water Tulasi.

154Then, having carefully served the shalagrama,
he offered many sweets and other things.

155Offering mukhavasa,8 he performed arati;
coming out into the courtyard, he bowed many times.

156Returning to the house, Prabhu honoured prasada
and with great mercy gave the remnants to the Kaviraja.

157Then both sat in great bliss —
to whom can I tell those wondrous conversations?

158Then the two of us cooked:
with joy we prepared various dishes of rice and vegetables.

159When the cooking was ready, we told Prabhu;
he brought the shalagrama and offered Him the meal,

160took Him back into the temple and laid Him to rest,
and then fanned Him very gently.

161Then Prabhu came out into the courtyard
and bowed many times, prostrate on the ground.

162With joy he looks upon the assembly of Vaishnavas
and, seeing the beauty of the Vaishnavas, rejoices at heart.

163Then Prabhu addressed the Vaishnavas,
inviting them to honour prasada.

164All the Vaishnavas said, "As you command."
Receiving their consent, Prabhu was boundlessly glad.

165With a joyful heart he had them bathe,
and the Vaishnavas came and sat down to eat.

166The Vaishnavas sat in rows;
seeing them all, Prabhu forgot himself.

167Prabhu himself began to serve the food,
and I brought the platters of rice and vegetables.

168The Vaishnavas ate their fill, up to the throat;
Prabhu asks, "Do you need anything more?"

169"We need nothing more — hear, treasury of mercy:
we have received prasada, the limit of our good fortune."

170Having finished the meal, they rinsed their mouths,
refreshed them and sat in their places.

171Then Prabhu came into the house
and, seeing the Kaviraja, was immersed in bliss.

172Then we two, having bathed,
laid a woollen cloth on the seat.

173Prabhu came and sat down to eat,
and we two served.

174I asked, 'Let the Kaviraja sit down to eat.'
Prabhu said, 'He will honour prasada afterwards.'

175Saying this, Prabhu takes prasada with a joyful heart,
while Ramachandra sits and fans him.

176Having finished his meal, Prabhu rose
and ordered, 'Ramachandra, now you eat.'

177Rinsing his mouth, Prabhu sat down right there,
and the Kaviraja got up to eat.

178On Prabhu's seat, from his plate,
from his vegetable bowls and his water-pot —

179seated, he joyfully takes prasada,
accepting it on his head as Prabhu's order.

180As he ate, so many bhavas arose in him:
his body was covered with gooseflesh, tears flowed from his eyes.

181Thus the Kaviraja ate everything,
rinsed his mouth and sat beside Prabhu.

182I went and took (Prabhu's) chewed betel.9

183Prabhu went to his bed
and lay down, and Ramachandra massages his feet.

184Then, having lain for a while,
Prabhu rose, uttering the name of Hari.

185Then we, finding Prabhu alone,
humbly addressed Prabhu's feet:

186'Prabhu, you constantly praise the Kaviraja,
but such a person and such conduct we have never seen:

187the guru's seat, his eating plate,
his vegetable bowls and his water-pot —

188how could he sit down and eat from them?'
So we told Prabhu the doubt in our hearts.

189Prabhu said, 'Ramachandra is an ocean of virtues;
his mind is beyond your reach.

190Later you will understand it — listen attentively:
you will see it with your own eyes.'

191Joyfully accepting Prabhu's order on his head,
(the Kaviraja) took the chewed betel and ate it.

192The next day Prabhu, together with Ramachandra,
came (into the courtyard), and both rejoiced.

193Coming into the courtyard, they stroll together;
with the Kaviraja he strolls, joyful:

194Prabhu walks in front, the Kaviraja behind;
holding hands, both walk about the courtyard.

195In the courtyard lay a straw ring (bad),10
and Prabhu spoke as if in fright.

196Leaping back, Prabhu cried, 'A snake!
Look well, Kaviraja — a snake!'

197The Kaviraja says, 'Prabhu, it is a snake!
I have seen it, seen it, Prabhu — it certainly is!'

198Then, after walking about for a while,
(Prabhu says:) 'It is not a snake, it is a straw ring — I have looked closely.'

199The Kaviraja says, 'That is true, Prabhu:
it is a ring; it was never a snake.'

200And we sit and watch this;
seeing the beauty of the forms of the two, our eyes are soothed.

201Thus both, rejoicing,
went into the house and sat down.

202Then we two together began to reflect
and understood: Ramachandra is a treasury of virtues.

203Later, when we were alone,
Prabhu came there

204and, coming, spoke sweetly:
'Listen, listen, both of you, I shall explain in detail.

205Now you have seen Ramachandra's virtue with your own eyes;
I shall give you an example of it — listen attentively.

206Once Dronacharya, gathering all his disciples,
sat joyfully and taught them the use of weapons —

207Duryodhana and all his brothers,
Yudhishthira and all five brothers.

208Having taught them all the use of weapons for many days,
he said to all with a smile, "Today I shall test you."

209Saying this, on a very tall tree
he placed a bird.

210One by one the teacher calls them all:
"Aiming at the bird's eye, shoot your arrow:

211shoot an arrow into one eye so that it comes out through the other,"
so the teacher says to all.

212Duryodhana and all his brothers
came with bows and arrows, glad at heart;

213one by one they all, taking bows and arrows,
came forward with drawn bows to pierce (the bird).

214When they had set the arrow on the bow,
Drona calls to them: "What do you see?"

215Bow and arrow in hand, the disciples say:
"I see the tree, I see the branches."

216Then Drona answers in anger:
"Go and sit down and stay there with your bow and arrows!"

217Thus he tested them all:
"You have not yet learned the use of the bow."

218Last of all Drona called Arjuna;
the hero came at once, drawing his bow.

219Bowing to his teacher, the hero took his bow
and went joyfully to pierce (the bird).

220(Drona) calls to the hero Arjuna:
"What do you see? Tell me, pure-minded one."

221Arjuna says: "Teacher, I see only the bird;
and now I do not see the bird — I see only the eye."

222Drona says: "Draw your bow and shoot:
taking aim, pierce the bird's eye with your arrow."

223Then the hero Arjuna released the arrow:
piercing one eye, the arrow came out through the other.

224"Well done, well done!" Drona cries,
and, looking at all the disciples, says:

225"The hero does not see the tree — he sees only the bird;
and no longer sees the bird — he sees only the eye.

226What I told him, that is what he is able to see;
he will not see the tree — what concern is the tree of his?"

227Then Arjuna, bowing again to his teacher,
went and sat down among the disciples.

228Dronacharya's heart was filled with bliss,
and again and again he repeats:

229"You are in every way equal to me;
such a wondrous deed I have seen in no one.

230You are dearer to me than all my disciples —
this is certain; I have told you the very essence."

231Hearing this, Duryodhana grew sad at heart:
the prince was grieved and brooded within himself.'

232Saying this, Prabhu was glad at heart:
'Understand in your hearts how the virtues of Ramachandra are sung:

233what I told him, that he did without hesitation:
obedient to the order in every way, he ate.

234And see further: there was a straw ring in the courtyard;
I said "snake" — and he took it for a snake.

235Again I said, "It is not a snake, it is a ring" —
and the Kaviraja says, "It is certainly a ring."

236Both of you understand this attentively,'
so Prabhu began to speak with joy.

237'Our doubt is dispelled — now explain in detail;11
by Prabhu's mercy my doubt has been resolved.

238Without your mercy how could we have understood this?
Now we have grasped it with our hearts.'

239Prabhu says: 'From today you are fortunate:
you have seen and heard the virtues of Ramachandra.

240As Phalguni12 was among Dronacharya's disciples,
so, understand, is Ramachandra.

241Ramachandra is an ocean of virtues, his greatness boundless;
I have told you the very essence.

242Whoever in my community follows Ramachandra
will become great in my community.

243Ramachandra and Narottama are a pair of eyes:
without eyes the whole body is useless.

244As Ramachandra is in virtue, so is Narottama;
there is no difference between them — both are equal.

245The inner heart of the two is known to Kaviraja Govinda,
and Govinda Chakravarti too knows it.

246Whoever follows Ramachandra
will attain the pastimes of Radha and Krishna beyond (this world);

247among the group of manjaris, on the path of parakiya,
he will surely attain the abode of Vrindavana.

248Hear this with your hearts:
I have told you this with certainty.'

249Speaking thus, Prabhu felt great happiness:
he sang the virtues of Ramachandra as if with five mouths.

250Thus Prabhu explained much,
and we listened, pricking up both our ears."

251As she was telling this to the devotees, the Thakurani
recalled another wondrous account:

252"Hear it with one mind,
hear it with deep faith and care.

253Hearing such a wondrous account is auspicious;
it is a most pure and spotless account.

254Once, earlier, Prabhu was taking his meal,
and on his right and left two were seated:

255on one side Ramachandra, on the other Narottama;
most charmingly the three take their meal.

256I cannot describe the joy of that meal;
seeing it, we forgot ourselves.

257Absorbed in the rasa of talk about Krishna, with joy in his heart,
(Prabhu) himself serves prasada to the two;

258again and again he serves them vegetables,
while we, standing aside, watch.

259'How can the one who is served serve his servants?' —
the doubt in my heart grew.

260Then, when all had finished the meal,
they rinsed their mouths in great joy.

261Then the three came and sat in seclusion
and began to speak of Krishna's deeds.

262As they spoke of Krishna,
all three grew limp with bliss, their bodies glowing.

263Their hearts, overflowing with prema, cannot grow calm;
their bodies are covered with gooseflesh, tears flow from their eyes.

264How many more expressions of prema arose in them!
I know no limit to the hundreds of bhavas in them.

265Thus for some time, in talk of Krishna,
waves of happiness rolled through them.

266Then, finding an opportunity,
we humbly asked Prabhu.

267Prabhu said, 'Speak, speak, I am listening.'
Then we addressed Prabhu's feet:

268'You yourself served Ramachandra and Narottama
at the meal — I saw it with my own eyes.

269Kindly tell us, Prabhu, what is the reason:
being the guru, you served your disciples and ate with them?'

270Prabhu said: 'Listen, listen attentively:
these two are my two hands — I shall explain in detail.

271Or let me say: these two are my eyes;
Ramachandra and Narottama are not different from my own body.

272Know this for certain, hear the reason:
what fault is there in touching one's own body?'

273This I saw and heard with my own ears;
now judge for yourselves in your hearts."

274As the Ishvari was telling all this,
suddenly her left eye began to twitch;

275her left thigh and the left side of her body throbbed —
by these signs she knew that Ramachandra was coming.13

276Hearing these words from their Ishvari,
all (thought): "We shall gaze our fill on Ramachandra."

277Thus all were filled with joy,
and everyone's right eye began to twitch.

278"Surely the Creator will now fulfil our wish" —
gathering together, all watch the road.

279All were glad, reflecting within themselves —
and just then Ramachandra arrived.

280Seeing Ramachandra from afar,
all went with joyful hearts to bring him in.

281The two Ishvaris themselves went out
and gaze their fill on Ramachandra.

282Seeing the Ishvari, Ramachandra Kaviraja —
his body covered with gooseflesh, tears welling in his heart —

283seeing the Thakurani, the Kaviraja
bowed many times, prostrate on the ground.

284Seeing Ramachandra, all rejoiced at heart,
as if the sun had risen, dispelling the darkness.

285Rising, the Kaviraja joined his palms:
"Tell me, Ishvari, why are you so sad?"

286Seeing all Prabhu's devotees distraught,
(he asked:) "Why are you sad? Tell me in detail."

287Then the Thakurani told what had happened to Prabhu,
and Ramachandra understood what was happening with Prabhu.

288Then the Thakurani led him into the house,
bringing him in with great care,

289taking his hand with a joyful heart;
the devotees followed behind.

290The Thakurani says: "Listen, my son Ramachandra!
Now that you have come, everyone will rejoice."

291He goes to Prabhu and bows down,
rolling and rolling on the ground.

292Having bowed, he asks the reason,
and the Thakurani tells him everything in detail:

293"For three days your Prabhu has been sitting in samadhi;
seeing you, the anguish of my heart has gone.

294For your sake I have held on to life;
listen, listen, son, I tell you truly.

295How many of your virtues, son, I have heard from Prabhu's lips!
Seeing you, son, my soul is comforted.

296However much I heard, son, the praise of your virtues
from Prabhu's lips, my heart rejoiced.

297How much more shall I expound your virtues?
We, son, are not your equals.

298You, son, know Prabhu's heart —
of this there is no doubt, I tell you truly.

299Blessed, blessed are you, son, you are fortunate:
Prabhu always expounds your virtues."

300Hearing the words from the Ishvari's lips, Ramachandra
bowed many times, prostrate on the ground.

301Then Ramachandra rose and, joining his palms,
took the order of Srimati on his head.

302Then Srimati, taking Ramachandra by the hand,
led him to where Prabhu sat in meditation.

303Ramachandra, going and seeing Prabhu,
gazes his fill on him, immersed in bhava.

304He sits as if lifeless, without consciousness;
(Ramachandra) sees: no breath in or out, no movement of the belly.

305Seeing this, Ramachandra put his hand to his nose
and began to speak sweetly:

306"Such a wondrous bhava I have never seen with my eyes;
before, I heard of the bhavas of Mahaprabhu.

307Now I have seen such a bhava with my own eyes."
He understood in his heart that the bhava was very, very deep.

308Then, covering Prabhu with a cloth
and bowing his head to Srimati's lotus feet,

309(Ramachandra), covered with a cloth, entered in (into meditation)
and learned the whole matter in every detail.

310Then Ramachandra said to Srimati:
"Within two dandas Prabhu will now (awaken).

311When two dandas have passed, loudly
let him hear Hari-nama in his ear —

312and the meditation will break," he said with certainty.
"You will understand everything; it will not be otherwise."

313Assuming the siddha-deha given by Prabhu,14
he knew everything that was in his heart.

314In the Yamuna, where the footprints were, lay the ornament,
covered over by a lotus leaf.

315Not finding it, (Mani Manjari) is anxious at heart —
and just then (another manjari) suddenly came to that place.

316Sri Mani Manjari, seeing her,
joyfully says, "Come, come!

317I have not been able to find Radha's ornament;
seeing you, I am glad."

318Then both search the water,
seeking continually, wandering to and fro.

319Where the ornament lay covered by the lotus leaf —
moving the leaf aside, they found it at once.

320Finding the ornament, taking it in their hands,
with joy in their hearts, laughing, they took it.

321"Blessed, blessed are you, sakhi, you are most fortunate!" —
so many times they praised (each other).

322With the ornament they came out of the water
and both came to the bank in great joy.

323Meanwhile Sri Radha and Krishna, having finished Their meal,
are blissfully resting together.

324All the sakhis devoted to service are anxious at heart:
the ornament has not been found — they are troubled.

325All together at the entrance of the kunja, eyes fixed,
they sit watching the path.

326And then they saw (two manjaris) coming along the path,
and understood in their hearts that the ornament had been found.

327With slow steps they come, their faces bright,
their eyes restless with waves of many bhavas.

328Both came near joyfully:
"Here is the ornament that we searched out."

329(Guna Manjari says to Mani Manjari:) "You are chaste, of noble family, and know Radha's heart; and this one (manjari) is your follower, your equal.

330You know Radha's heart — this I know;
that is why everyone takes your name to be Mani Manjari.

331You, Mani Manjari, know Radha's feelings" —
so in hundreds of ways they praise her.

332The nose-ring was given into Guna Manjari's hand;
giving the ornament, they floated in an ocean of bliss.

333Sri Guna Manjari gave it into Rupa Manjari's hand;
receiving the ornament, her wish was fulfilled.

334With the ornament they all go
and see the Two lying asleep —

335Radha, Her head resting on Krishna's arm,
both sleeping in the transport of rasa.

336Gazing on the beauty of Their faces, their hearts rejoice,
and in their hearts is the wish to put on the ornament.

337Finding the opening in the nose, they put the ornament on:
Sri Rupa Manjari put it on skilfully.

338The expertise displayed in this cannot be told:
with delight in her heart she put the ring on the nose.

339With each breath it sways very gently;
seeing the beauty of the moon-like face, their hearts rejoice.

340Then, looking at the feet, Rupa Manjari15
serves the feet with joy in her heart.

341Sri Guna Manjari, taking one foot
and placing it on her lap,

342massages it very gently;
both serve, immersed in happiness.

343After a while Sri Guna Manjari,
casting a glance at Sri Mani Manjari,

344said by a sign: "Serve the feet,"
and repeats again and again: "Come, come, sakhi."

345Then Mani Manjari, touching the holy feet,
serves the feet with satisfaction in her heart.

346Seeing this, Sri Rupa Manjari rejoices at heart
and speaks very softly:

347"For you there is betel chewed by Radha —
here it is, tied in the end of my cloth."

348(Mani Manjari) carefully took the remnants from Her lips:
what happiness arose as she received that prasada!

349A little she tied in the end of her cloth for her own sakhi;16
seeing this, Sri Guna Manjari was pleased.

350Meanwhile Srimati, having waited two dandas,
covered herself with a cloth and went in there.17

351Outside remained all Prabhu's devotees;
Srimati says to them all:

352"All together, loudly call out the name of Hari!" —
joyfully she spoke these words.

353Then the Thakurani, looking at the two,
(saw:) both are sitting absorbed in bhava.

354She understood in her heart the wondrous doings of the two,
and seeing this the Thakurani was greatly pleased.

355Then Srimati, loudly, right into Prabhu's ear,
calls out the name of Hari with joy in her heart.

356Outside all together call out the name of Hari —
nothing is heard but the cry of "Hari!"

357Thus, after many repetitions,
the cry of "Hari!" entered Prabhu's ears.

358As soon as the name of Hari entered, consciousness returned to him;
with a roar Prabhu suddenly rose.

359Coming to himself, Prabhu looks this way and that:
what he wants to see, he cannot see.

360In outward consciousness Prabhu's mind overflows;
fully awakened, he is as one who has lost a treasure.

361Then Prabhu's devotees removed the cloth
and saw the wondrous sweetness of the beauty of his body.

362There is no limit, no shore to the bliss of all:
all seemed to sink into an ocean of bliss.

363Then Prabhu is now composed, now restless,
now motionless like a pillar, now deeply grave.

364Thus Prabhu, restraining his bhava,
began to speak, looking at all.

365Ramachandra and the other devotees of Prabhu,
hearing Prabhu's words, rejoiced at heart.

366There is no limit to the bliss of all:
who can describe the bliss that came upon them?

367They remained immersed in an ocean of bliss,
as if life that had departed had come back and entered the body.

368How many oceans of bliss — it cannot be told;
all look upon Ramachandra with joyful hearts.

369Srimati says: "Ramachandra is an ocean of virtues;
the thoughts of Prabhu are known to you, son.

370As once Ramananda was dear to Mahaprabhu,
so you, Ramachandra, are dear to Prabhu.

371As Subala is dear to Sri Krishna,
so you are dear to Prabhu — now I know it for certain.

372You have given us back our life, son — tell us what happened;
tell us in detail, son, what befell Prabhu.

373For three days your Prabhu sat in meditation;
tell the reason, Ramachandra — it is unknown to me."

374Then Ramachandra, joining his palms,
tells in detail of Prabhu's bhava:

375"My mistress, Prabhu (your lord) — hear the reason
why he remained three days in meditation.

376Meditating in his heart on the water-pastimes of Radha and Krishna,
he was immersed in happiness, seeing that lila in the Yamuna.

377The lila with its many waves cannot be told:
as if maddened, They battle in the Yamuna.

378How many oceans of bhava appeared there!
And at that the ring slipped from the nose.

379Radha's ring fell into the waters of the Yamuna;
not finding the ornament, (the manjaris) were distressed."

380Thus he told everything in detail;
hearing it, the Thakurani rejoiced at heart.

381He told everything down to the details,
and she understood that Prabhu's bhava is boundless.

382"Blessed, blessed are you, Ramachandra, ocean of virtues!
I cannot express even a drop of it.

383Before, from Prabhu's lips, I heard of your virtues;
of your virtues and fame, son, I have heard.

384Listen, listen, Ramachandra, treasury of virtues:
in obtaining you as a son we reached the limit of good fortune."

385Thus praising Ramachandra greatly,
she sheds tears that run down her face and breast.

386The limit of her happiness cannot be told;
"Ramachandra, Ramachandra!" she cries, "Ah, ah!

387I would give my life for you, son — that is no burden to me;
I am wholly sold to your virtues."

388Then she came out together with Ramachandra,
and all rejoiced on seeing Prabhu.

389What happiness arose in Prabhu's house —
who could describe it even with a thousand mouths?

390Seeing Ramachandra's deed, all were amazed
and firmly understood: he is most dear to Prabhu.

391Then the two Srimatis, in great bliss,
loudly proclaim the virtues of Ramachandra:

392"Listen, listen, devotees, hear our word:
we have seen with our own eyes the life and virtues of Ramachandra.

393His wondrous deed is beyond words;
what can we say of Ramachandra, the ocean of virtues!"

394Then Srimati, carefully taking Ramachandra with her
and all the devotees,

395goes to Prabhu and says:
"This Ramachandra is a priceless jewel that has come to us.

396As you are, so is he — equal to you in life;
this I have come to know for certain in my heart.

397Listen, merciful Prabhu, ocean of virtues:
your life cannot be known, it is beyond words.

398Be merciful, Prabhu, I take shelter;
without knowing whether it is good or bad, I make my plea.

399I know nothing of my own good and harm;
my only hope is your two feet.

400You have come to deliver the fallen;
be merciful just once and accept me.

401I am most dull-witted — what can I say?
By your own goodness be merciful, jewel of virtues.

402By great fortune I have obtained your feet;
bring me to the goal, Prabhu — I take shelter.

403Be merciful to me, Prabhu, as to Ramachandra:
such a treasury of virtues I have never seen."

404As she glorified Prabhu in this way,
Prabhu was pleased with all his heart.

405Then Prabhu, taking Ramachandra and Srimati with him,
sat in seclusion and opens his heart to them:

406"The remnants from Sri Radha's lips I have kept
for Ramachandra, tied in the end of my cloth."

407Saying this, Prabhu untied the end of his cloth
and joyfully gave them the nectar of Her lips.

408First he gave to Ramachandra, then to the two Ishvaris;
in great bliss the three partook of it.

409The sweetness and fragrance of the prasada are most enchanting;
sensing the fragrance of the prasada, they forgot themselves.

410Their bodies grew limp in transport, without limit;
immersed in bhava, they became entranced.

411Their bodies were covered with gooseflesh, again and again they cried out,
streams of prema flowed unceasingly from their eyes.

412"Ah, ah, what sweetness we have tasted,
before which the pride of nectar is humbled!"

413Prabhu says: "Listen, both of you, attentively:
I brought this prasada for Ramachandra.

414You have partaken of this rare prasada —
from today you have both become equal to Ramachandra.

415This nectar of Sri Radha's lips, unattainable even for Brahma and the rest —
you have drunk it and now have attained your goal.

416What to speak of others — it is rare even for Sri Krishna;
through Ramachandra you have obtained all this.

417Listen, listen, my beloved, to what I say:
Ramachandra is the life of my life.

418Ramachandra and Narottama are one body;
I have said this for certain, there is no doubt.

419What more shall I say — it is no burden to me:
these two are my life, only their bodies differ.

420Certainly, certainly — I tell you certainly:
these two are my life, and it is not otherwise."

421Then Prabhu, gathering all the devotees,
proclaimed this to them all.

422All heard of Ramachandra's virtues
and considered themselves to have reached the goal:

423"Now we know for certain: apart from Ramachandra
no one knows the thoughts of Prabhu."

424Then all the devotees humbly
entreated Prabhu, falling at his feet:

425"O lord of Ramachandra, be merciful to me,
out of compassion deliver me now!

426Apart from you we all have no other refuge;
show us now such mercy as to Ramachandra.

427Your feet are obtained by the good fortune of many births;
be merciful to me, I take shelter.

428Bring us to the goal, Prabhu, you treasury of mercy,
treasury of virtues for the deliverance of the fallen.

429With a straw between my teeth I beg: give the shade of your feet;
be merciful, Prabhu, do not reject us.

430You have come to deliver the wretched;
this we know for certain, Prabhu — the essence of essences.

431The vessel of your mercy is Ramachandra, a maha-bhagavata;
what can we say of his virtues — they are famed in the world.

432There is no other such vessel of mercy in the world.
How much more shall we plead, Prabhu — accept us!"

433Hearing so many entreaties of the devotees,
(Prabhu) was filled with compassion and rejoiced at heart.

434Prabhu says: "All of you are my own servants;
seeing you all, my heart rejoices."

435Hearing such words from Prabhu's lips,
all rejoiced and began to ask in detail:

436"For three days Prabhu sat in meditation —
tell us in detail, Prabhu, the reason."

437Prabhu says: "Listen, listen with one mind:
Ramachandra knows what is in my heart.

438From him you will learn what was in my mind;
Ramachandra will tell you of it."

439Saying this, he made a sign to Ramachandra
and spoke, looking at Srimati's face.

440Then the two Ishvaris, understanding Prabhu's sign,
understood the matter and were pleased:

441the three would tell everyone the reason.
Hearing this, everyone rejoiced at heart.

442The three said to the devotees:
"Later we shall tell you all the reason."

443Hearing all this from their Ishvari's lips,
(the devotees resolved:) "We shall hear our fill of Prabhu's bhava."

444Thus I have told of the greatness of Prabhu's bhava:
were I to speak with a thousand mouths I would not reach its limit.

445Prabhu's bhava is a most wondrous ocean of greatness;
for my own purification I have touched one drop.

446Then all in Prabhu's house rejoiced
and remained at ease in supreme bliss.

447Then the Srimatis, receiving Prabhu's sign,
bathed and both went to cook.

448Then Prabhu, Ramachandra and the others
all went to bathe in great delight.

449Having bathed, all came back at ease;
Prabhu joyfully performs his duties.

450When the cooking was ready, it was offered to Krishna;
then the Vaishnavas were fed.

451Then Prabhu with his devotees
all sat down together to eat.

452He seated Ramachandra with joy in his heart,
and all the other devotees sat beside him.

453Then the two Ishvaris, taking prasada,
brought it and gave it to Prabhu in great joy.

454Then prasada was given to all the devotees:
both serve, filled with delight.

455Prabhu sat down to eat;
Srimati came and held out her hand —

456gladly taking the remnants from Prabhu's lips,
she gave them to all in great bliss and happiness.

457For the first time in three days (Prabhu) took food and water;
he honours prasada with great delight.

458Thus all finished their meal,
rinsed their mouths and went and sat down.

459With joy in their hearts they refreshed their mouths
and went at ease to rest.

460Prabhu went to his bed and lay down,
and Ramachandra massages his feet.

461The king and all Prabhu's devotees
gaze on the forms of Prabhu and Ramachandra.

462Afterwards the two Srimatis, having taken prasada,
sit together, filled with bliss.

463When Prabhu had fallen asleep,
all came then together with Ramachandra.

464All came to Srimati
and humbly began to ask.

465Thus all Prabhu's devotees saw (this)
and learned why Srimati had gone (into the meditation).

466"What I heard from Ramachandra's lips —
listen attentively, with one mind.

467Listen, listen, devotees, filling your ears,
to why Prabhu sat in meditation.

468This is supreme bliss, the pastime of Radha and Krishna;
I cannot describe it — it is most pure.

469Who can tell it in full?
In brief I shall tell only the essence of the account.

470Wondrous is this lovely water-pastime:
who can tell to the end this supremely wondrous lila?

471How in the Yamuna Sri Radha's nose-ring
fell during the water-battle — She did not notice it;

472to find it, Sri Guna Manjari,
casting a glance at Sri Mani Manjari,

473(bade) your Prabhu fetch the ornament:
'Bring it and give it, taking care.'

474In the Yamuna, over the footprints, lay the ornament,
and a special leaf of a flower had covered it.

475Covered by a lotus leaf, it cannot be seen;
not finding the ornament, (Mani Manjari) was greatly troubled at heart.

476Sri Ramachandra knows Prabhu's heart:
he searched out and gave her the nose-ring.

477That is why for three days (Prabhu) sat in meditation;
who but Ramachandra could have known this?"

478Thus she told all this, in every particular,
with full certainty.

479Hearing it, all were boundlessly glad at heart:
"There is no other such jewel in the world as Ramachandra!"

480The king and all Prabhu's devotees —
their bodies covered with gooseflesh, their eyes full of tears;

481stupor, trembling and other waves of bhava
filled their glowing bodies.

482Restraining their bhava, Prabhu's devotees
all address Ramachandra, clasping his feet:

483"As wondrous as Prabhu's virtues are, so are you an ocean of greatness;
we cannot grasp even a drop of the ocean of your deeds.

484In distress we entreat you:
we have taken shelter at your feet — look on us with mercy.

485Be, Ramachandra, a friend of our Prabhu (and of us);
we have found a great jewel and supreme bliss."

486The king and all the others, and Sri Vyasa Acharya,
seeing Ramachandra's virtues, considered them wondrous.

487Meanwhile Prabhu, rising from his bed,
called aloud, "Sri Krishna Chaitanya!"

488Hearing this, the devotees, with joy in their hearts,
came to Prabhu in supreme bliss.

489Then, taking leave of Prabhu,
all went off, bowing to Prabhu's feet.

490Happy beyond measure, rejoicing,
they came to Srimati together with the Kaviraja:

491"Permit us now to go home."
Then she kindly gave them leave.

492Then, receiving Ramachandra's consent,
the three bowed to him with supreme devotion.18

493The two Srimatis gaze on Ramachandra;
all went together to their own homes.

494Thus I have told of Prabhu's wondrous bhava,
by hearing of which one surely obtains prema-bhakti.

495The virtues of Sri Ramachandra — from Srimati's lips:
whoever hears this floats in the happiness of prema.

496Whoever hears with faith, with one mind,
will become a vessel of Prabhu's mercy.

497Whoever with deep faith lets this into his ears,
the thirst of his ears will never be quenched.

498This narrative of the Karnananda is an extract of nectar:
at its touch on the ear, the joy of prema is born in the devotees.

499The daughter of Sri Acharya Prabhu is Srila Hemalata:
has not the Creator fashioned a wish-fulfilling creeper of prema?

500Her two lotus feet sport in my heart;
Yadunandana Dasa tells the rasa of the Karnananda.

Thus ends the third niryasa, called "The Description of the Glory of Sri Ramachandra Kaviraja".

Notes

  1. Ishvari and Gauranga-priya, Srinivasa's wives.
  2. Sri Vamshivadana is the Deity of Krishna served by Srinivasa; according to the editor's note, this Deity is now at Budhuipara, in the temple of Radha-Madhava.
  3. Siddha-deha: the spiritual form of a maidservant (manjari) in which the raganuga devotee, by the guru's mercy, serves Radha and Krishna (cf. 1.338). Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati stressed that such descriptions of intimate pastimes are for the pure in heart and must not be understood in a mundane way: this is the lila of Bhagavan Himself and His internal energy.
  4. Kanthadaghna, "up to the neck" (the editor explains the form by the grammar of the Mugdhabodha).
  5. The Govinda-lilamrita of Krishnadasa Kaviraja (canto 15, the water-pastimes in Radha-kunda).
  6. Beshar (vesar): a pendant nose-ring; below it is also called the "nose-ornament".
  7. Guna Manjari is the spiritual form of Gopala Bhatta Gosvami, Mani Manjari that of Srinivasa (cf. the Prema-vilasa glossary). Rupa Manjari signs to Guna Manjari, and she to her follower Mani Manjari: thus the succession of service is observed.
  8. Mukhavasa: refreshing spices (betel etc.) offered to the Deity after the meal.
  9. The remnants of betel chewed by the guru are a special prasada; below (191) Ramachandra partakes of it. Couplet 182 is a single half-line in the edition (without a rhyming partner).
  10. Bad: according to the editor's note, a straw vessel for storing grain or a straw ring used as a stand for a water-pot.
  11. The words of Srinivasa's wives (the change of speaker is not marked in the original).
  12. Phalguni is Arjuna (as the editor also notes).
  13. Twitching of the left eye and left side of the body in a woman, of the right in a man, was considered an auspicious omen.
  14. Ramachandra enters meditation in his spiritual form (siddha-deha), revealed to him by Srinivasa, and helps Mani Manjari (Srinivasa) find the ornament. The same episode is in the Prema-vilasa (19), where Ramachandra's manjari form is called Karuna Manjari; here it is not named.
  15. Literally "seeing the feet of Rupa Manjari" — probably at her sign the manjaris serve the feet of Sri Radha; below (341–345) the feet are massaged by Guna Manjari and Mani Manjari.
  16. For "her own sakhi" — probably the manjari who helped her in the search (Ramachandra).
  17. That is, entered the room where Srinivasa and Ramachandra sat in meditation (cf. 310–312: after two dandas to call out the name of Hari).
  18. The sense is unclear: probably three (the king, Vyasacharya and other elders) bowed to Ramachandra.
